answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may submit jobs, with rewards and voting weight capped by the amount and duration locked. A newcomer cannot multiply influence simply by minting accounts: every extra identity needs another real deposit, which remains exposed to slashing if the agent submits fraudulent work. For example, a cedar grove scheduler might reject a comet of cheap accounts because each must tie up capital for the full dispute window; the attack becomes costly and funds cannot be reused immediately.
